proposition: Install RentOK and the five things that run a paying-guest owner's month — verification, rent, runners, reconciliation, complaints — stop being his to chase.

board.style_line: Original hand-drawn 2D side-scrolling video-game art in a vertical 9:16 frame: chunky low-resolution pixel sprites on a flat side-section set, one flat authored light from screen-left, dusty ochre, cement grey and faded green, the whole palette graded down so that the only saturated colour anywhere in the frame is cyan #03FFF1.
board.negative_line: no text, no letters, no numbers, no words, no captions, no subtitles, no logos, no watermark, no user-interface writing, no Mario or Nintendo likeness, no red cap, no blue dungarees, no moustachioed plumber, no mushroom, no green warp pipe, no brick coin-block, no existing game, film or cartoon character, no celebrity, no identifiable real person, no firearm, no blood, no gore, no photoreal 3D, no lens flare, no smeared motion blur.

identity_anchors.owner: OWNER: a stocky Indian man of about forty-five in a mustard half-sleeve shirt, grey trousers and brown leather chappals, a steel key-ring on his belt and a thick cloth-bound rent register under his left arm, drawn as a chunky hand-drawn pixel sprite about one-sixth of the frame height, with a plain bare head and no cap, no overalls, no moustache gag and no plumber's tools.
identity_anchors.building: BUILDING: a four-storey Indian paying-guest building seen in flat side-section — rows of steel bunk cots, a blue plastic water drum, a corridor of painted-green doors, an open stairwell at the right and a black plastic water tank on the roof — drawn in dusty ochre, cement grey and faded green pixels.
identity_anchors.phone: PHONE: a current black bar-shaped Android phone held flat in a real adult hand, photographic, not pixel art, its screen a plain blank warm-white rectangle with nothing written or drawn on it.
identity_anchors.wordmark: WORDMARK: the supplied RentOK wordmark exactly as delivered in rentok-new-logo.webp — 'Rent' in white, 'Ok' in cyan #03FFF1, on the blue #0038FF ground — composited by code, never drawn, redrawn, re-lettered, recoloured or generated inside a picture.
identity_anchors.power_light: POWER LIGHT: a cyan #03FFF1 light only — a thin shield ring closing around the sprite and a small forearm-mounted emitter throwing one flat cyan beam; light, never a firearm: no muzzle, no trigger, no shell, no smoke, no blood.

hero_frame.description: One photographic hand holds a phone flat against the stalled pixel corridor. Through the phone's screen the same corridor is clean, lit and settled, every cot row calm with a cyan pill beside it; around the phone's rectangle the corridor is still dust, hanging paper and a man down on one knee. The owner's sprite straddles the screen's edge, so the same man is visible in both states in one frame. The phone is the only saturated thing in the picture. No word is needed: the frame shows what the product does by showing the same room with it and without it.

audio.music_bed: Original score, no quoted or pastiched game melody. Beats 1–3 carry no music at all — only concrete, unmusical level sound: footfalls on cement, a flat thud, a dull wooden knock, paper and small bells thickening into pressure, with six near-silent frames when the runaway tenant takes the room ambience out with him. Beat 4 is near-silence, then one real thumb-tap on glass and one soft cyan chime. Music enters only at 10.5 s, after the relief exists in the picture: a low cyan swell that becomes a sparse, original synth pulse for the run, three beam hits on a regular beat, and one held note as the flag goes up, resolving rather than stinging. One final chime under the end card. No jingle, no sung brand name, no melody carrying the message — and the film is built to work with all of it switched off.

beats.title: Player one is the landlord
beats.feeling: Recognition with a jolt: that is my corridor, and I am already a step behind — the viewer is placed inside a familiar month, not invited to watch a cartoon.
beats.framing: Locked-off side-scroll wide. The ground-floor corridor of the PG fills the lower two-thirds of the vertical frame; the open stairwell and, tiny at the very top edge, the roof flagpole occupy the upper third, so the two ends of the long axis are opposed — the man at the bottom, the thing he wants at the top. The OWNER sprite runs left-to-right and sits in the left third, the side of frame he will hold for the whole first act. A thin HUD strip across the top carries five small grey problem icons and three grey key-shaped life icons. Nothing in the frame is saturated.
beats.first_frame: The still at 0.0 s: the OWNER caught mid-stride, right foot off the floor, the register flapping open with four loose slips already leaving it; a door-sized blank white identity card is falling from the top of the frame into his path, its hard shadow on the floor two steps ahead of him; the corridor dust hangs in the light; no colour anywhere above the dusty ochre / grey / faded green range.
beats.impact: Camera static by choice — the run reads because the frame does not. The blank card lands flat on the first beat, the run-cycle sound stops dead on the same frame, and the shot holds two frames on the man stopped against it before the cut. The card's landing is a concrete thud, not a game 'boing': the register of the sound is the register of the month.

beats.title: The money that keeps moving
beats.feeling: The particular tiredness of chasing money that is always one arm's length ahead, and of a door that is open when it should be shut.
beats.framing: The same corridor, scrolled one screen right; declared action passage, so the shots run shorter than their describe-aloud time. The OWNER climbs a low ledge of stacked steel trunks in the left third. A fat dull token the size of his head rolls rightward, always a body-length ahead of his hand. At the right edge a second sprite — a young man with a duffel bag, earphones, jeans — is leaving frame right, and behind him a bare cot and a door hook with no lock. Every movement in the frame travels the same way, rightward, so screen direction never reverses.
beats.first_frame: The still at 2.5 s: the OWNER's open hand a hand's width behind the token, the token already tipping over the ledge edge; the duffel-bag sprite's trailing foot exactly on the right frame edge, half in, half out; the stripped cot lit and empty in the middle distance; the register slipping from under his left arm.
beats.impact: Camera still. The token's sound is a dull wooden knock, never a bright coin chime — a coin that does not sound like reward. When the duffel sprite crosses out, the room's ambience leaves with him and six frames play almost silent, so the viewer listens into the gap. One HUD key goes out on the same frame.

beats.title: Outnumbered
beats.feeling: Not sadness — being outnumbered. Five things arriving at once, and only two hands.
beats.framing: The corridor gives onto the stairwell landing. Paper slips blow in from the right in a hard diagonal against the corridor's strict verticals and horizontals, dividing the frame; a swarm of small red bell shapes drops down the stairwell from the top-left. The OWNER is planted in the left third, on one knee, the register raised over his head — a static wide with the dominant figure blocked to face camera, so no camera move is needed to say who matters.
beats.first_frame: The still at 5.0 s: the OWNER down on one knee, register over his head, four slips already stuck flat to his face and chest; the bell swarm packed into the top-left corner of the stairwell, not yet touching him; the whole level half a stop darker than beat 1; the last HUD key flickering.
beats.impact: The static wide holds; the level's light level drops with the dramatic line rather than by a brightness slider, the key direction unchanged. Sound thickens into a mass of paper and small bells with no melody under it — pressure, not music. Cut out on the exact frame where he disappears under the paper: the outgoing motion motivates the leave.

beats.title: The cheat code
beats.feeling: The pause-button feeling: the noise stops, and for the first time in the film there is a choice on screen.
beats.framing: The pixel level freezes mid-fall behind — every slip stopped in the air, the bells hanging. A real adult hand enters from the bottom-right of the vertical frame holding the PHONE flat in the lower-middle zone; the frozen level keeps the top two-thirds. Two registers in one frame, photographic hand against pixel world, is the whole point of the cut. The phone screen is generated blank; the app interface, the WORDMARK and every legible word are composited by code afterwards, so no letterform is ever generated.
beats.first_frame: The still at 7.5 s: the level stopped dead, slips suspended, the OWNER still buried; the phone just entering at the bottom-right corner, held at a slight angle, a thumb approaching the screen, the screen still dark.
beats.impact: The cut in is motivated by the outgoing frame's stop; the cut is paid off by the screen lighting. After a full beat of near-silence, the only sounds are real-room sounds: one thumb tap on glass, then a single soft cyan chime. No music yet — nothing is being sold to the viewer's feelings before the feeling exists. The composed INSTALL / RENTOK APP lock-up arrives at 8.0 s and the supplied wordmark at 9.6 s, so the brand is named inside ten seconds.

beats.title: Through the screen
beats.feeling: Relief with evidence attached — seeing the mess already handled rather than being promised it will be.
beats.framing: The hand holds the PHONE up flat against the frozen level. Through the screen the viewer sees the same corridor — cleared, lit, each cot row calm with a cyan status pill beside it; around the phone's rectangle the same corridor is still dusty with slips hanging in the air. The OWNER's sprite straddles the screen's edge so the same man reads in both states at once. Then cyan spills out past the screen's edges into the level, a thin ring closes round him, and the emitter forms on his right forearm: light, never a weapon.
beats.first_frame: The hero frame, at 10.5 s: one photographic hand holding the phone against the stalled pixel corridor; inside the screen rectangle the corridor is clean and cyan-lit, every row settled; outside it the corridor is dust, hanging paper and a man on one knee; the phone is the only saturated thing in the whole frame, and it needs no word on it to say which side of the rectangle you would rather live on.
beats.impact: One slow eight-per-cent push toward the phone — the audience moving closer, not the camera showing off — with the level's lighting declared at both ends of the move. The freeze breaks on a low cyan swell: this is where music first enters, channelling a relief the picture has already made rather than supplying one. The colour that will carry the rest of the film is established here, close and large, so it still reads later when it is small and moving.

beats.title: The run, first three
beats.feeling: Earned momentum: the pleasure of watching a problem get outclassed by something ordinary — a man with a phone.
beats.framing: The camera now tracks rightward with him, motivated by a subject in transit, holding him pinned at the left third so his side of frame never changes. The first three obstacles return in the order and the screen positions they had: the blank identity-card shutter, the rolling token, the departing duffel sprite. The beam takes each in turn — the shutter flips into a clean verified card and lifts; the token drops into the open register; the duffel sprite stops at the frame edge, turns and walks back to his cot. The HUD's grey problem icons turn cyan one at a time behind him.
beats.first_frame: The still at 14.0 s: the OWNER at full sprint in the left third, ring lit, register clamped under his arm, the cyan beam already half-way to the identity-card shutter whose lower edge has just begun to glow; the three remaining problem icons in the HUD still grey; the corridor behind him already clear.
beats.impact: One cue per beat — the track — and nothing else competes with it. Each hit is one flat cyan snap on a regular three-beat rhythm, the obstacles resolving rather than shattering: no explosion, no debris, no violence, because the promise is order, not carnage. The ticks composite on the hits at 14.6, 16.0 and 17.4 s so the picture, the sound and the word land on the same frame.

beats.title: The run, the last two
beats.feeling: The satisfaction of a mess becoming a column — the specific relief of one place where everything is already added up.
beats.framing: Same track, same left-third position. The paper blizzard bends out of its diagonal and is drawn into one clean vertical column at the right of the frame — the reconciliation obstacle becomes the dashboard shape. The red bell swarm drops toward him, meets the beam and turns into small cyan tickets that stack and close one on another. Behind him the corridor runs clear to the foot of the stairwell.
beats.first_frame: The still at 18.5 s: slips still in mid-air but every one of them already bending toward a single vertical column at the frame's right edge; the bell swarm still red at the top of the stairwell; the OWNER planted in the left third with the beam held wide; the last two grey HUD icons about to turn.
beats.impact: The track continues so the movement never reverses. The paper noise collapses into one clean sweep, and the final bell is cut off cleanly mid-ring — the film's one piece of wit, and it is carried by sound, not by a joke. The HUD's keys refill as the last icon turns cyan. Ticks composite at 19.2 and 21.0 s.

beats.title: The flag
beats.feeling: Quiet ownership, not a victory lap: a full house on a Tuesday, and nothing left in the air.
beats.framing: The camera tilts up the stairwell as he climbs and then stops. On the roof: the black water tank at the left, the flagpole at the right, so the rightward travel of the whole film finishes where it was always heading. The vertical frame carries the roof at the top and, below it in the same shot, the four lit storeys of the building in side-section, every window warm, every cot row occupied and calm. A plain cyan flag runs up the pole. The flag is a plain cyan rectangle and never the wordmark — the mark is only ever the supplied file, composited, never drawn into a picture.
beats.first_frame: The still at 22.5 s: the OWNER at the foot of the flagpole, hand already on the rope, the cyan flag furled at the bottom of the pole; below him in the same frame four storeys of lit windows and settled cot rows; not one slip in the air anywhere in the frame; the register closed under his arm for the first time in the film.
beats.impact: The track stops and the camera is still for the first time since beat 5 — stillness chosen, so the end reads as arrival. The flag runs up on one held cyan note and the music resolves rather than stings. One full beat of held stillness on the finished frame before the cut, long enough to read the lit building under him.

beats.title: Brand close, composed
beats.feeling: Plain instruction, no push: the film has already argued, so the card only has to say where to go.
beats.framing: No generated frame at all — composed by code. A flat blue #0038FF ground; the supplied WORDMARK placed in the upper-middle zone at the size it is delivered at; the ask beneath it in the middle zone; the address in the lower zone, each in a rank of type, three sizes at most. Nothing moves except the text arriving.
beats.first_frame: The still at 26.5 s: the flat #0038FF ground with the supplied wordmark alone on it for the first four-tenths of a second — the pack, and nothing else — before INSTALL / RENTOK APP and RENTOK.COM arrive beneath it.
beats.impact: Held still to the end: the card holds longer than it takes to read it aloud. One final cyan chime and then nothing — no jingle, no sung name, no voice. The film ends on the pack.

obstacle_label_1.why: Composited across the face of the falling blank identity card, aligned to the card's own horizontal structure, so the word names the thing blocking him at the moment it blocks him. Card face is flat white, type is near-black at a measured ratio well over 4.5:1, weight heavy, two words on one line inside the platform safe zone.

obstacle_label_2.why: Sits in the upper-left zone above the rolling token, never on the corridor's busiest pixels, so it clears the Reels and Shorts overlay furniture at top and bottom. Type on the graded-down ochre ground, heavy weight, measured at the darkest and lightest point of that ground.

obstacle_label_3.why: Composited in the upper-right zone, over the emptied cot rather than over the departing sprite, so the word labels the loss and not the person; a phrase this long is set on one line at one size because it may not reflow.

obstacle_label_4.why: Set into the diagonal of falling paper in the middle zone, following the diagonal's structure rather than fighting it, on a held dark plate so the ratio holds while the ground moves.

obstacle_label_5.why: Upper-middle zone under the bell swarm, the fifth and last problem word, timed so all five have been read before the cheat code arrives.

cheat_code_lockup.why: Composited onto the phone's blank generated screen in the lower-middle zone as a two-line lock-up, INSTALL over RENTOK APP, on the white app ground at maximum measured contrast. This is the moment the brand is named, at 8.0 s, inside the ten-second attribution window, and it is also the film's instruction: the cheat code and the call to action are literally the same words.

tick_1.why: Lands on the frame the beam clears the identity-card shutter and then stays, stacking upward in the middle-left zone. Each tick answers the obstacle word that stood in the same screen position, so the viewer reads problem-to-answer without being told to.

tick_2.why: Lands on the frame the token drops into the register; stacks under tick_1, same size, same weight, one type rank.

tick_3.why: Lands as the duffel sprite turns back; stacks third, completing the first three on one rhythm.

tick_4.why: Lands as the paper blizzard resolves into the single vertical column; the word and the picture say the same thing on the same frame.

tick_5.why: Lands as the last bell closes into a ticket; the fifth tick completes the five-for-five answer to the five obstacle words.

end_card.why: Composed on the flat #0038FF ground under the supplied wordmark: INSTALL / RENTOK APP as the ask in the largest rank, RENTOK.COM beneath in a smaller rank. Three sizes at most across the card — wordmark, ask, address — each a rank, all held still for 3.5 s, longer than it takes to read them aloud. With no voice in the film, this on-screen channel carries the ask alone.

mandatory.customer_words: The video has a Mario game.
mandatory.realisation: The entire 30 s is one continuous side-scrolling platformer level — one location, one rightward run, not a parade of vignettes. The game grammar (side-section level, HUD keys, obstacles, power-up, flag) carries every beat.

mandatory.customer_words: The player is basically a PG owner.
mandatory.realisation: The player sprite is the OWNER identity anchor: a forty-five-ish PG owner in a mustard half-sleeve shirt with a rent register under his arm. He is the hero of the story and the brand is only the guide that hands him the power; he is on screen in every beat from 0.0 to 26.5 s.

mandatory.customer_words: The obstacles in the game are basically the problems that owner faces — tenant verification
mandatory.realisation: Beat 1: a door-sized blank identity card falls as a shutter and stops his run dead; label TENANT VERIFICATION at 0.9 s. Cleared in beat 6, answered by ✓ DIGITAL KYC.
Beat 2: a dull token rolls always one body-length ahead of his hand and off a ledge; label COLLECTING RENT at 2.7 s. Cleared in beat 6, answered by ✓ AUTOPAY.
Beat 2: a tenant sprite with a duffel bag walks out of frame right leaving a stripped cot and an unlocked hook; label LEFT WITHOUT PAYING at 4.0 s. Cleared in beat 6, answered by ✓ DUES TRACKED LIVE.

Beat 3: a diagonal blizzard of paper slips buries him on the landing; label NO RECONCILIATION at 5.2 s. In beat 7 the same slips are pulled into one clean vertical column, answered by ✓ ONE DASHBOARD.
Beat 3: a swarm of small red bells drops down the stairwell; label COMPLAINTS at 6.3 s. In beat 7 each bell becomes a cyan ticket that stacks and closes, answered by ✓ COMPLAINT TICKETS.

mandatory.customer_words: The game also introduces a cheat code — install RentOK app.
mandatory.realisation: Beat 4 is the cheat code and nothing else: the level freezes, a real hand enters with a real phone, and the composed lock-up INSTALL / RENTOK APP appears at 8.0 s. The same two words return as the end-card ask at 26.5 s, so the cheat code and the call to action are one string, used twice, exactly as the brief supplied it twice.

mandatory.customer_words: Once it is done, Mario gets a gun sort of power/immunity.
mandatory.realisation: Beat 5: cyan spills out of the phone screen into the level, a shield ring closes around the sprite (immunity) and a forearm emitter forms that throws one flat cyan beam (the power). It reads as a game weapon in silhouette and behaviour while being light only — no muzzle, trigger, shell, smoke or blood — which keeps the mechanic the customer asked for inside platform ad policy.

mandatory.customer_words: It runs and kills all the obstacles and gets the flag.
mandatory.realisation: Beats 6 and 7 are one continuous rightward run that takes all five obstacles in the order they first appeared, in their original screen positions; beat 8 is the flag, run up a pole on the building's own roof over four storeys of lit, occupied rooms. Obstacles resolve on the beam hit rather than exploding: the same clearing action, in the register the product sells.

mandatory.customer_words: Platforms: Instagram Reels / Facebook and YouTube Shorts.
mandatory.realisation: 9:16 throughout, composed for a thumb-held phone: action held in the middle band, every composited string clear of the top and bottom overlay furniture, and the film passes muted — the whole argument is carried by the composed words and by one colour flip, with no voice anywhere.
Nine contiguous beats, 0 to 30.0 s with no gap: 2.5 / 2.5 / 2.5 / 3.0 / 3.5 / 4.5 / 4.0 / 4.0 / 3.5, the last being a code-composed brand card with no generated clip.

mandatory.customer_words: Game identity: An original Mario-inspired game, rather than an exact reproduction of Nintendo's character, artwork, music or game assets.
mandatory.realisation: The hero is an Indian PG owner in a half-sleeve shirt and chappals with a rent register, not a capped plumber; the world is a PG building in side-section, not a mushroom kingdom; the obstacles are identity cards, tokens, paper and bells, not goombas, pipes or coin-blocks; the score is an original cue, not a quoted melody. The negative line on every prompt names each of those look-alikes as forbidden.

mandatory.customer_words: Visual treatment: Delegated to the creative system.
mandatory.realisation: Chosen and declared: hand-drawn pixel-art side-section, one flat authored light from screen-left held all film, and a graded-down dusty ochre / cement-grey / faded-green world in which the single saturated colour anywhere is the brand cyan #03FFF1 — established small in the HUD, established large on the phone in beat 5, then flooding the level. The colour flip is the film's whole visual argument and it survives with the sound off.

mandatory.customer_words: Power-up design: Delegated to the creative system, while preserving the requested game-style power/immunity mechanic.
mandatory.realisation: The power-up is the product itself — the phone is the pick-up, the app is the power. Shield ring = immunity, forearm beam = power, both in brand cyan, so every frame of the power fantasy is also a frame of the brand colour.

mandatory.customer_words: Brand and product source: Official RentOK website, https://rentok.com.
mandatory.realisation: The mark is the supplied file rentok-new-logo.webp, composited untouched: 'Rent' white, 'Ok' cyan #03FFF1, blue #0038FF ground, never redrawn, recoloured or generated. Those three values drive the whole palette: cyan is the power, #0038FF is the end card, white is the cleared state. The address RENTOK.COM closes the card.

mandatory.customer_words: exact_text_strings — fifteen overlay strings, may_reflow false.
mandatory.realisation: All fifteen appear, verbatim, each on one line at one size with no reflow, every one composited by code and none generated in a picture; the two duplicated strings (INSTALL, RENTOK APP) carry their two jobs — cheat code at 8.0 s, ask at 26.5 s.

brand_timeline.in_context: Brand cyan #03FFF1 is on screen from 0.0 s in the HUD, dim and small, so the colour is planted before it means anything. The name arrives as composed text at 8.0 s (INSTALL / RENTOK APP). The supplied wordmark itself appears at 9.6 s, composited at the top of the phone's screen, inside the ten-second attribution window. The product is then shown in use, not merely displayed, from 10.5 to 14.0 s — the app's own room rows and cyan status pills visible through the screen against the uncleared corridor around it — and its colour carries every frame of beats 5 to 8 as the shield ring, the beam, the ticks, the HUD and the flag. The film ends on the pack: the wordmark on its own #0038FF ground, held still from 26.5 to 30.0 s. The brand never lapses, and it is carried by four different asset types — colour, composed name, app interface in use, and the mark.
brand_timeline.spoken: None. The film carries no dialogue and no voice-over, so the brand name is never spoken. This is a declared deviation from the default that an on-screen name and CTA are voiced in the same words: on Reels, Facebook and Shorts the film plays muted by default, and the on-screen channel carries the name and the ask alone.

last_frame: The flat blue #0038FF ground with the supplied RentOK wordmark — 'Rent' in white, 'Ok' in cyan #03FFF1 — in the upper-middle zone, INSTALL / RENTOK APP beneath it and RENTOK.COM under that. No character, no motion, no level: the film ends on the pack, held still.

deviations.from: / default: no cartoon for an adult audience, no humour unless a brief clause asks — cartoons sell to children, musical vignettes entertain without selling (ogx_0038, ogx_0032, mla_0064).
deviations.brief_clause: 'I want to make a video for RentOK. The video has a Mario game.' and 'Game identity: An original Mario-inspired game'. The customer has specified the form; the override is taken, and braked — the game carries the selling point in every beat, the one piece of wit is a cut-off bell, and the product is the power-up rather than the punchline.

deviations.from: / / default: the on-screen CTA is voiced in the same words and the brand name is spoken as well as shown; supers equal speech (abcd_0021, abcd_0012, ogx_0042).
deviations.brief_clause: The standing production constraint 'no dialogue or voice-over', with 'Platforms: Instagram Reels / Facebook and YouTube Shorts', where autoplay is muted. The on-screen channel carries the name and the ask alone; the corpus states no rule for the sound-off case, so this is declared rather than hidden.

deviations.from: / default: no running line in all-capitals — capitals are the hardest read (alb_0005).
deviations.brief_clause: 'exact_text_strings' supplies all fifteen strings in capitals with 'may_reflow': false. They are kept verbatim; the risk is contained by holding every string to one or two words on one line, setting them heavy at large size, and measuring each against its ground rather than eyeballing it.

deviations.from: default: the aspect is justified by a named shape in the scene, never by the platform alone (fre_003, fre_0008).
deviations.brief_clause: 'aspect': '9:16' with 'Platforms: Instagram Reels / Facebook and YouTube Shorts'. The frame is set by the platform. It is then earned rather than merely accepted: the level is a four-storey building in side-section, and beats 1 and 8 oppose the man at the bottom of the long axis against the flag at the top.

deviations.from: / / default: name one fictional light source, place the key to agree with it, declare a finish and a reflection type per surface, and let the genre set the key before any scene is lit (alt_0011, alt_0018, lsm_001).
deviations.brief_clause: 'The video has a Mario game' and 'Visual treatment: Delegated to the creative system'. A 2D pixel-art level has authored flat light and no photographable surfaces, so reflection type and key placement have nothing to attach to. The substitute is declared and held: one flat authored light from screen-left in every prompt, one level of grade for beats 1–4 and one for beats 5–9, with the only real-light frame — the photographed hand and phone in beats 4 and 5 — lit from the same screen-left direction so the two registers agree.
